card.summary: The Environmental Health Restoration Act of 2026 directs the Environmental Protection Agency to reinstate specific environmental and public health regulations, guidance, and enforcement programs that were in effect on January 19, 2025. It prohibits federal officials from weakening or delaying these standards without explicit congressional authorization. Furthermore, the bill mandates the restoration of scientific advisory boards, use of the social cost of carbon, specific enforcement funding levels, and environmental justice programs.
card.title: Environmental Health Restoration Act of 2026

latest_action.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

summary: The Environmental Health Restoration Act of 2026 requires the Environmental Protection Agency to reinstate specific environmental and public health regulations, programs, and guidance that were in effect on January 19, 2025. The bill sets restrictions against future deregulatory delays, mandates the use of peer-reviewed science and specific values for the social cost of carbon, restores scientific advisory boards, sets enforcement funding floors, expands environmental justice programs, and allows private citizens to bring civil actions in federal court if the agency fails to comply.

affected_groups.effect: Must reinstate numerous prior environmental regulations, staff scientific advisory panels, conduct public health impact assessments, issue annual enforcement reports, and maintain funding and staffing minimums for enforcement.
Must comply with reinstated federal standards regarding emissions, reporting, and pollutants, and are barred from having advisory board members with financial or advisory ties to them.
affected_groups.group: Regulated Industries (including power plants, oil and gas operations, and vehicle manufacturers)

affected_groups.effect: Receive prioritized monitoring, permitting oversight, and enforcement from the EPA under environmental justice provisions.
Granted the ability to bring civil actions in U.S. district courts to compel compliance with the Act and potentially recover attorney's fees.
affected_groups.group: General Public and Adversely Affected Persons

key_provisions: Requires the EPA Administrator to reinstate all regulations, guidance, and enforcement programs in effect on January 19, 2025, regarding greenhouse gases, methane, mercury and air toxics, greenhouse gas reporting, hazardous air pollutants, PM2.5 particulate matter standards, and vehicle emissions.

Prohibits the President, the EPA Administrator, and other federal officials from delaying, suspending, repealing, weakening, or granting exemptions to these reinstated regulations unless explicitly authorized by Congress.

Mandates the reconstitution and full staffing of the Science Advisory Board and the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee with members not financially or advisory-wise associated with regulated industries, and requires regulatory decisions to be based on peer-reviewed science.
Restores the use of the social cost of carbon in rulemakings, specifying a 2 percent discount rate and a value of $190 in 2020 dollars per metric ton.
Authorizes appropriations of $10,993,653,000 for fiscal year 2027 and subsequent fiscal years, adjusted annually for inflation, to support EPA duties and maintain an enforcement personnel floor.

Directs the EPA to restore and expand environmental justice programs, prioritize monitoring and enforcement in communities with disproportionate pollution burdens, and conduct public health impact assessments.
Establishes a private cause of action allowing any person adversely affected by the Administrator's failure to comply with the Act to bring a civil action in a U.S. district court.
missing_information: Specific economic outcomes or cost estimates beyond the authorized appropriations amount and the specified social cost of carbon value.
Projections on the exact number of personnel affected or specific timelines for court cases.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Environmental Health Restoration Act of 2026 requires the Environmental Protection Agency to reinstate specific environmental and public health regulations, programs, and guidance that were in effect on January 19, 2025. The bill sets restrictions against future deregulatory delays, mandates the use of peer-reviewed science and specific values for the social cost of carbon, restores scientific advisory boards, sets enforcement funding floors, expands environmental justice programs, and allows private citizens to bring civil actions in federal court if the agency fails to comply.
summary_detail.significance: The bill mandates a large-scale legal and operational rollback of actions taken by the EPA since January 20, 2025, committing billions in annual appropriations and granting new legal enforcement mechanisms to private citizens and states.
